content_voiceover: This table gives more granular pharmacologic detail for the four DOACs, apixaban, dabigatran, edoxaban, and rivaroxaban, using their brand names Eliquis, Pradaxa, Lixiana or Savaysa, and Xarelto respectively. Time to peak concentration ranges roughly from one to four hours across all agents, and half-life in patients with normal renal function ranges from about eight to fifteen hours. Hepatic impairment matters differently by drug, moderate hepatic impairment, Child Pugh B, has no consistent effect on exposure for apixaban, dabigatran, and edoxaban, but increases rivaroxaban exposure by 2.3-fold, which is clinically important. Renal excretion also varies substantially, dabigatran is renally cleared at 80%, by far the highest, making it the DOAC most affected by renal impairment, while apixaban is only 25% renally excreted, making it often preferred in renal insufficiency. Dosing frequency differs too, apixaban and dabigatran are twice daily, while edoxaban and rivaroxaban are once daily. All DOACs interact with P-glycoprotein, and apixaban and rivaroxaban additionally interact with CYP3A4. For boards, the renal excretion percentages and the rivaroxaban hepatic impairment exposure increase are frequently tested details.
keypoints: Dabigatran has highest renal excretion at 80%, most affected by renal impairment
Apixaban has lowest renal excretion at 25%, often preferred in renal disease
Rivaroxaban exposure increases 2.3-fold in moderate hepatic impairment
Apixaban and dabigatran are BID; edoxaban and rivaroxaban are once daily
keypoint_voiceover: Remember these clinical pearls. Dabigatran has the highest renal excretion at eighty percent, making it most affected by renal impairment. Apixaban has the lowest, at twenty-five percent, so it is often preferred in renal disease. Rivaroxaban exposure increases 2.3-fold with moderate hepatic impairment. And dosing frequency differs, apixaban and dabigatran are twice daily, while edoxaban and rivaroxaban are once daily.
